tasks.short: Copy score parts for individual performers

steps.what: Identify the correct score version and required parts for individual performers
Copy the specified score parts into individual performer documents
Proofread copied parts for notes, rests, cues, layout, and performer readability

tasks.design: Configure native part extraction in the notation application {OTHER} from a checked symbolic score. Keep score identification, extraction choices, and performer-readable proofing with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Copying can repeat notes that already exist in a machine-readable score.
tasks.enabler_now: Notation applications can extract specified parts without reinterpreting the music.
tasks.still_hard: Source errors, missing cues, awkward page turns, and unclear multi-voice notation.
tasks.human_edge: The director judges whether a formally correct part can actually be used in rehearsal.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated copying may leave more time for part proofing.

reach.learn: Cueing, page turns, and notation conventions

evidence.claim: Native notation part extraction can reduce exact copying from a checked symbolic score; this is an E1 design estimate.

assumptions: Boundary covers copying unchanged parts, excluding original composition, adaptation, and musical transposition decisions. OTHER is the notation application.

Composer or existing score provider produces the symbolic source through unchanged work before s1. Director checks source version and captures staff or voice identifiers, passage boundaries, target part names and layout choices in s1; capture remains counted. Paper-only or ambiguous scores require manual copying unless conversion effort is separately measured and included.
Test native part extraction before custom code. Existing automatic extraction receives no new saving. Final proofing remains fully counted; no unreviewed public release occurs.
research_questions: Does extraction reduce active effort after source checking and full rehearsal-part proofing are included?

incremental.description: Maintain extraction settings and check recurring layout faults

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55; gross 45 minus 8 upkeep gives net 37. Range assumes a checked symbolic source and genuine current copying; paper-only scores or existing extraction may save nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Define tour dates, venue needs, accommodation requirements, and transport constraints
Coordinate bookings or engage a touring company and confirm the resulting arrangements
Compile the tour itinerary from confirmed concert, venue, accommodation, and transport details
Verify itinerary connections and circulate the agreed tour information

tasks.design: Compile an itinerary in {DOCS} from booking details the director has confirmed in {PROJECT}. Retain tour choices, supplier coordination, company selection, connection checks, and final circulation with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Itinerary documents can repeat confirmed booking information held elsewhere.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project fields and document templates can populate an itinerary without making bookings.
tasks.still_hard: Viable connections, cancellations, performer needs, and reliable supplier commitments.
tasks.human_edge: The director negotiates practical trade-offs and spots an itinerary that is formally complete but unworkable.
tasks.altitude: Less itinerary copying; touring decisions and external commitments remain unchanged.

reach.task: Check an itinerary against confirmed bookings
reach.learn: Travel buffers, venue access, and contingency planning

evidence.claim: A template can compile an itinerary from explicit confirmed booking fields; this is an E1 design and does not automate tour negotiation or booking.

assumptions: Boundary is director tour coordination, including the alternative of hiring a touring company. Supplier and touring-company fulfilment remain separate unchanged work; shifting coordination to a supplier is not treated as a saving.

Director captures booking identifier, confirmed date and local time, location and verified address, supplier contact, travel segment, reservation reference, status and source timestamp in s2. Supplier confirmations arrive during s2 before itinerary compilation; capture and clarification time remain counted.
Missing or conflicting addresses, times or confirmation status are flagged as unresolved and handled manually. No structured address or availability flag is inferred from free text.
Test native project fields and itinerary templates before custom code. No purchase, booking change, or itinerary circulation is automated.
research_questions: Does itinerary compilation reduce active effort after verified source capture and connection checking are included?

already_counted.description: Check itinerary feasibility and circulate the agreed version

incremental.description: Maintain itinerary mappings and check recurring booking-field errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact itinerary version, booking references, times, locations and distribution recipients; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=85; gross 15 minus 5 upkeep gives net 10. Range assumes several confirmed tour stops and repeated document copying; highly disrupted tours may save nothing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep current with music and music technology

steps.what: Study current music and technology trends through listening, reading, and professional exchange
Try relevant music technology and assess its practical musical value

tasks.design: Retain critical listening, reading, professional exchange, and tool trials. Existing sources in {DOCS} and music tools in {OTHER} support learning without treating a digest as equivalent musical understanding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Novel tools and trends need direct experience to assess their musical relevance.
tasks.enabler_now: No automated substitute for professional learning is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Separating useful developments from fashionable claims and unsuitable tools.
tasks.human_edge: The musician judges relevance through listening and practical musical experience.
tasks.altitude: Professional learning remains part of the musician's work.

reach.task: Discuss a new tool's musical and technical limits
reach.learn: Signal quality and practical workflow testing

evidence.claim: Critical listening and practical technology assessment remain human learning; no labour saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is professional learning and limited trials, excluding production experimentation for a specific composition. OTHER is the existing music playback and trial toolset.
Publishers, musicians and tool providers supply existing source material; the director reads, listens, and tests during these steps. No new structured trend feed or capture work is introduced.
Native source access and trial tools remain sufficient; unchanged practice adds zero incremental upkeep.
research_questions: Which developments remain useful after practical testing in the musician's own work?

incremental.description: No new system or process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net saving zero. Critical learning and hands-on trials remain unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The music director can reduce exact part copying and itinerary assembly while retaining musical proofing, touring choices, and professional learning.
role.ambitious_version: A director who gives performers reliable parts and travel information while keeping artistic and logistical decisions accountable.
